analysis:
Reviewed GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift (base/head) and KVPoolReclaimer.swift (patch/base). The change is availability/performance memory management: it adds an idle-gated sweep window (closed/idle/pressure), a releaseRetained hook that asks CBv2 engines to drop retained free KV segments, a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP=0 rollback env, an engine-refusal reclaim signal (signalsEngineRefusals, directChargeRefusalSignal), and a new init parameter 'environment'.

Security observations: No change to encryption, attestation, authorization, coordinator protocol, or the SSD prefix cache's at-rest format, HMAC naming, TTL or KEK handling (T-041 mitigations unchanged). The new releaseRetained path discards retained KV segments but does not touch the on-disk cache. Idle-gated sweep keeps the MLX buffer pool warm while engines serve, so freed KV buffers may persist in the GPU cache longer than before until idle, pressure or load-gate release (touches T-028 residual-GPU-memory posture; threat model already treats this as in-process memory within the provider's trust boundary and the operator-memory adversary under T-011/T-014 is unaffected in kind). Environment variables are read from the provider's process environment (operator-controlled, same actor as other DARKBLOOM_* switches), so no new trust boundary. The reclaim flush still revalidates isReclaimAllowed (native-owner fault guard) before the GPU callback; the new flushIfDue(flush) only records lastReclaimAt after a flush actually ran, and the idle path uses performIfIdle so it declines rather than blocks admission. Rate limiting is preserved. Overflow is handled in proactiveWindow.

Unverified integration points: CBv2RetainedKVSegments, EngineV2Factory.segmentRetentionEnabled, WholeMacServiceBudget.isIdle/performIfIdle, and EngineProcessMemoryOwner(onRefusal:) are outside supplied evidence; their correctness (e.g. no deadlock, release actually zeroing/dropping memory) is not verified. No concrete security regression identified.
